To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Asthma Illusion Representation Scale (AIR©) is a valid and reliable tool for assessing parents' asthma illness representation (IR) and that IRs aligned with a professional model of asthma care are associated with improved asthma management and health outcomes.

(1) The AIRS© has acceptable psychometric properties in a predominantly ethnic minority, inner-city sample; (2) AIRS© scores are associated with asthma severity, asthma symptoms, and acute asthma-related health care utilization; and (3) AIRS© subscales are associated with asthma-related healthcare provider and parent relationships.

the AIRS© instrument has good internal reliability and external validity and can be used to differentiate parents based on ethnicity (white, African American, Puerto Rican, Afro-Caribbean), poverty, and education (less than high school).

we have validated a new tool, the Asthma Illusion Representation Scale© (AIRS©), that is a quick and efficient way to assess the parent’s perception of asthma and their child’s asthma.
the AIRS© instrument is a useful tool to identify areas of discord between the parent's and HCP's asthma management plan.

the AIRS© instrument is a valid and reliable measure of asthma IRs and that parents' perceptions of their child's asthma are important to consider in the management of the disease.
